title: Branching in-memory version history
instructions:
Implement a small git-like history using two cooperating modules. No filesystem
I/O is needed; file contents are strings in an in-memory working tree.

## Files
- `snapshot_store.py`: validated, detached file snapshots.
- `version_history.py`: editable working tree and parent-linked history.

`snapshot_store.py` API:
- `validate_path(path: str) -> None`: accept a nonempty relative slash-separated
  path whose segments are nonempty and neither `.` nor `..`. Reject backslashes
  anywhere. Invalid paths raise `ValueError`. Other characters, including spaces,
  are allowed. Assume paths are strings.
- `SnapshotStore()`, `save(files: dict[str, str]) -> int`, and
  `load(snapshot_id: int) -> dict[str, str]`: IDs start at 1 and increase by one per
  successful save, even for identical snapshots. Validate every path as above;
  non-string contents raise `TypeError`. A failed save consumes no ID. Copy input
  and output dictionaries. Loading an unknown ID or an ID whose exact type is not
  `int` raises `KeyError` (including bool). Assume save receives a dict.

`version_history.py` exposes `History()` with a public `head` attribute, initially
`None`, and these methods:
- `write(path: str, content: str) -> None`: validate path and string content by the
  store's rules, then create or replace the file in the working tree.
- `delete(path: str) -> bool`: validate path; remove the file and return whether it
  existed.
- `files() -> dict[str, str]`: a detached copy of the working tree.
- `commit(message: str) -> int`: strip outer whitespace and require a nonempty
  message, else raise `ValueError`. Save a snapshot, record the old head as parent,
  move head to the new ID, and return it. Assume a string message. Empty working
  trees and commits with unchanged contents are allowed. IDs begin at 1 and are
  never reused. Invalid commits leave head, working files, and ID allocation alone.
- `checkout(commit_id: int) -> None`: restore that commit's entire snapshot and
  set head to it, discarding uncommitted edits. Invalid IDs follow `load`'s rules
  and leave all state unchanged. Any existing commit remains available, even if
  it is no longer an ancestor of head.
- `log(limit: int | None = None) -> list[dict]`: follow parents from head, newest
  first. Each detached dict has exactly `id`, `message`, and `parent` (an integer
  ID or `None`). An empty history returns `[]`. `None` means no limit; zero means
  `[]`; negative limits raise `ValueError`. Assume limit is None or an integer.

After checking out an older commit, a new commit has THAT commit as its parent;
`log()` must follow ancestry, not sort all commits by ID. Work stays in memory.
